title: Austin Progress: Lights, Hospital, Citizen Claims
summary:
*   **Infrastructure Upgrades:** Authorized a new street lighting system for Lavaca, 19th Streets, and University Avenue. Also, fixed street centerlines and sidewalk widths for several other key areas.
*   **New Hospital Building Progress:** Increased the local architect's compensation for the upcoming City Hospital project and officially appointed Leslie N. Iredell to oversee its construction.
*   **Citizen Claims and Financial Matters:** Approved payments for a horse injury ($10) and a significant legal judgment (over $800) against the city, while also rejecting another claim and cancelling an erroneous property assessment.

Regular meeting of the City Council: Austin, Texas, November 21, 1912.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The minutes of the
last regular and subsequent recessed meetings were read and adopted.
Reports of City Officers:
The Mayor laid before the Council the reports of the City Sexton, the Supt of the Water &
Light Plant for the month of October 1912, also that of the Plumbing Inspector for the
months of August, Sept & Oct 1912, which were read and ordered filed. Unfinished business:
The Mayor laid before the Council a resolution authorizing the Supt Parks and Public
Property to equip and install a street Lighting system on Lavaca, 19th streets and on
University Avenue, and making an appropriation to install said system, which resolu-tion
was introduced and read at the last regular meeting of the Council, and laid over until
this meeting. The resolution was passed by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge,
Councilmen Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Councilman Hart offered the following resolution : Whereas, it appearing to the City
Council that by a resolution passed on the day of November ,1912, appointing H B Thomsen
Architect for the new City Hospital Building, the compensation of the local Architect or
Inspector ,to be selected jointly by the City and H B Thomsen, Architect, to supervise the
work from its inception to comple-tion,was by agreement by the City and H B Thomsen , the
Architect, fixed at one % of the 5 % allowed the Architect, and the City desiring an
efficient representative to be upon the ground to superintend the construction of said
building and all preparatory work in connection therewith ; and believing that one per
cent (1%) of the contract price of said building is not adequate compensation for an
efficient Superintendent for the services to be performed and required of him: Therefore,
Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin: That an additional one per cent
(1%) of the contract price of said building be and the same is hereby allowed for the
services of said local architect or inspector, making the total compensation of two per
cent (2%) of the contract price of said building, 1% being paid by H B Thomsen, architect,
as recited in said resolution, and 1% by the City, as recited in this resolution.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Councilman Hart presented a report from the City Marshal to whom was referred a claim of N
Jackson, for pay for horse killed by the City authorities, stating that he had
investigated said claim, and recommending that same be not allowed.
On motion the report was adopted and the claim rejected by the following vote; Yeas Mayor
Wooldridge, Councilmen Bartholomew,Hart,Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

The Council then recessed until this P M.

November 21st P M.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Whereas, J R Morris makes
affidavit ,whic affidavit is hereti attachedand made a part hereof,that he did not on the
first day of January 1912,ner at any prior or subsequent approximate dates,own vendors
lien notes in the amount of $ 2,400.00 nor any other such sum;
Now Therefore,

.Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That the assessment of $
2,400.00 of vendors lien notes against J R Morris for the year 1912, be and the same is
hereby cancelled,and the Assessor and Collector of the City of Austin is hereby authorized
to take credit upon his rolls for the year 1912,by said amount.
The resolution was adopted by the followingvote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew,Hart,Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Councilman Powell offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of
the City of Austin,Texas,that the sum of $ 10.00be appropriated to pay Douglass McQuirter
for the injuries to his horse received in falling in a hole in the bridge across the
ravine on 14th street ,said claim to come out of the claim and damage fund,and that the
City of Austin,Texas, be released from further damages by paying this claim.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew,Hart,Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

The Council then recessed subject to call.
